stories.headline: Russian diesel not for us, but for world markets, says US President Donald Trump
stories.bodyText: Washington: Facing criticism over the diesel deal with Russia, US President Donald Trump said the fuel from Moscow's refineries was meant to stabilise the global market, which has been hit by high prices. On October 9, Trump announced that Russia would supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel, followed by an additional 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons "immediately thereafter." To facilitate the shipments, the US Treasury Department issued a temporary licence easing sanctions on Russian diesel shipments to global markets until April 7, 2027. The move came ahead of November congressional midterms in the US, as diesel prices surged amid supply disruptions caused by the Iran war. "That's a diesel deal. Not for us. That's being released into the world. That's not being released to us," Trump told reporters here on Tuesday, amid a growing chorus against the surprise deal he announced last week after talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin. .India faces 100% US tariffs for buying Russia, Iran oil. Republicans and Democrats hit out at the deal, which Trump announced three weeks after the US Congress authorised him to impose sweeping sanctions on Russia and slapped tariffs on its key trading partners, including China and India. "That's a diesel deal that's going to be released into the world for the world market, because the world market suffered with high prices. And when you knock out diesel refineries, that's not a great thing. But they are not releasing it to us. They are releasing it to the entire world," Trump said. On Tuesday, a bipartisan group of US senators wrote to Trump, terming the Russia deal a "gift to our adversary and a betrayal of our allies". "The deal you struck with President Vladimir Putin on October 9 will not achieve just ends, nor will it benefit Americans," the senators said. The letter was signed by Democrats Richard Blumenthal, Chris Coons, Dick Durbin, Jack Reed, Jeanne Shaheen and Sheldon Whitehouse and Republicans Alan Armstrong, Susan Collins, John Cornyn, Mitch McConnell, Lisa Murkowski and Thom Tillis. "This deal is a gift to our adversary and a betrayal of our allies; it should be rescinded," the letter said. Senators said they recognised the need to lower energy costs for Americans, but asserted that allowing Russian diesel into global markets will offer limited to no relief to Americans. The deal "only provides Putin with more fuel to finance his war machine and enables Russia to continue its brutal attacks on Ukrainian civilians," they said. "It will have a negligible impact on fuel prices, but the revenues the Kremlin will receive from this agreement will undoubtedly finance its desired war of attrition and advance its security cooperation with China, Iran, and North Korea," the senators said. Last month, Congress passed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which Trump swiftly signed into law. "Both chambers passed the legislation with resounding, bipartisan votes, clearly demonstrating our intent and granting you the authorities to broker a just and fair peace," the senators said. They said these authorities require the president to apply economic pressure on Russia and the chief enablers of its war, particularly China, thereby enhancing the US negotiating position to bring a swift end to this ruinous conflict.

stories.headline: Houthis target Saudi Aramco compound, limited fire reported
stories.deck: A missile attack targeted Saudi Aramco's administrative building, damaging upper floors of the headquarters complex. Authorities reported intercepting multiple missiles and drones aimed at various regions, including Riyadh. In Riyadh, fragments from intercepted missiles injured four individuals and damaged several homes. This incident follows a series of Houthi missile attacks against Saudi…
stories.bodyText:
Saudi Aramco’s administrative building in Dhahran was hit in a missile attack that triggered a limited fire, Saudi Arabia’s energy ministry said on Wednesday, as the kingdom faced a fresh wave of Houthi missile and drone attacks.
No casualties were reported in the incident, while Saudi authorities said they had intercepted missiles and drones targeting several parts of the country.
A company source told Reuters that a ballistic missile struck the Aramco headquarters complex, damaging the top three floors of an office tower. The complex houses a major operations centre overseeing the state-owned oil giant’s network of onshore and offshore oil rigs, pipelines, refineries and export terminals.
The energy ministry said authorities responded to the incident late on Tuesday and took the necessary measures.
The Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed a missile over Dhahran, with fragments falling in a residential area. Authorities also reported intercepting and destroying missiles and drones targeting the capital, Riyadh, and Saudi Arabia’s southern region.
In Riyadh, four people, including two women, a man and a child, were injured after fragments from two intercepted Houthi missiles fell in the capital, Saudi civil defense said on Wednesday. The debris also caused limited damage to 15 homes, a civil defense spokesperson said.
The latest attacks follow a series of Houthi strikes on Saudi targets over the past week. Riyadh’s international airport has faced four strikes, including a ballistic missile attack on Saturday that killed 13 people.

stories.headline: CJP’s Das, Ranka, Shinde under preventive arrest over Jantar Mantar trespass
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Delhi Police have arrested Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) activists 
Saurav Das
, Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde and others for allegedly trespassing at the Jantar Mantar protest site in New Delhi.
According to police sources, the activists have been taken into preventive custody, as cited by ANI.
The group's legal team head Ratna Singh said the activists would be produced before a court on Wednesday.
"Delhi Police arrests Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, and Ajinkya Shinde at Parliament Street Police Station in today’s Jantar Mantar case. Trespass, bond violation, obstruction of public official’s duty, etc. They’ll be produced before the SCM Court in the morning. A possibility of Judicial Custody (JC) in the Tihar Jail is possible. They were not allowed to meet their lawyers till late at night. They were brought to Parliament Street PS at 3 AM in a private van. Despite these illegal actions, their spirits are high," Singh said in a post on X.
"Update at 5.38 am - Just been informed that Saurav, Ashutosh, and Ajinkya are likely to be produced before the SEM at Mandir Marg Police Station within one hour. 
FYI, 24 hours timeline will end soon," she said in another post.
Earlier, Ratna Singh accused Delhi Police of acting arbitrarily and following orders from senior officials in its handling of the CJP activists. She also said that the they were denied access to lawyers for nearly 24 hours and were not initially informed of the grounds for their detention.
"We are currently witnessing the Delhi Police operating according to a specific 'rulebook', one dictated by orders from above. They set the law aside to follow this rulebook. We saw how people who went to Jantar Mantar, simply to hoist the Tiranga, were detained. It has been nearly 24 hours, yet they have not been allowed to meet any lawyers, nor have they been initially informed of the grounds for their detention or arrest," she said.
Singh further alleged that police personnel had denied lawyers and volunteers access to the detained party members despite repeated attempts to meet them.
"They denied access not only to ordinary volunteers but also to lawyers who had been present since morning. The SHOs and other officers on site kept insisting they were acting under orders from above. Who, then, is issuing these orders to the Delhi Police, orders that override the law itself?" she asked.
She also criticised the police for their handling of law and order in the national capital, alleging that peaceful protesters were being stopped from holding demonstrations while criminals continued to roam freely.
"We see criminals roaming freely, wandering the city, assaulting people, yet peaceful protesters are being stopped. Designated protest sites are being 'de-notified,' and people visiting these public spaces are being detained without explanation and held in custody for extended periods," Singh said.
"The Delhi Police is being used as a puppet, and they are dealing very harshly with peaceful protesters, which is not right," she added.
The development comes amid an ongoing agitation by the CJP and Opposition parties against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.
CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde were detained on Tuesday by Delhi Police while attempting to enter Jantar Mantar, and a case was registered against them. The action came a day after authorities de-notified the site as a designated protest venue.

Following the de-notification of Jantar Mantar, authorities designated Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in east Delhi as alternative venues for protests and demonstrations.
The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) had constituted a committee to examine alternative locations where citizens could exercise their right to organise protests. Based on the committee's recommendations, Jantar Mantar was de-notified as a designated protest venue, according to the notice.

stories.headline: Indian airlines cancel flights to Saudi Arabian cities till Oct 17
stories.deck: While announcing cancellation of flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah till October 17, Air India also said it was closely monitoring and assessing the developments in the region to resume safe operations
stories.bodyText:
IndiGo, Air India Express, Air India, and Akasa Air on Tuesday (October 13, 2026) announced cancelling flights connecting Saudi Arabian cities till October 17 in view of the evolving situation in the Gulf country.
There have been attacks in Saudi Arabia, including at the Riyadh airport, in recent days.
IndiGo, in a post on X on Tuesday (October 13, 2026), said that due to the evolving situation in Saudi Arabia, flights to and from Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah stand cancelled until October 17.
"In view of the evolving situation in the region, we have cancelled flights to and from Dammam, Jeddah and Riyadh until 17 October. Affected guests are being offered complimentary rescheduling or a full refund on cancellation. We continue to monitor the situation closely," Air India Express said in a statement.
While announcing cancellation of flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah till October 17, Air India also said it was closely monitoring and assessing the developments in the region to resume safe operations.
The airline, in a post on X, said it was offering a full refund on cancellation for the affected passengers.
Akasa Air said that in view of the escalating security situation in the West Asia and the associated risks to safe flight operations, it has extended the suspension of all flights to and from Riyadh and Jeddah until October 17.
"This decision follows a careful assessment of the evolving situation, with safety remaining the primary consideration. We continue to closely monitor developments and assess the situation in real time," it said in a post on X.
Last week, the airlines had temporarily suspended services to Riyadh in the wake of attacks at the city's airport reportedly by Houthi militants.
The hostilities between the Iran-backed Houthi group and Saudi Arabia have escalated. There have been attacks with armed drones and missiles.

briefs.headline: Club manager, aides beat driver to death for spilling beer on his wife
briefs.deck: A 29-year-old driver named Daljeet Singh was killed after an altercation at a club in Delhi. The incident began when he accidentally spilled beer on the club manager's wife during her birthday celebration. Following a violent confrontation, Daljeet and his friends were assaulted by the club staff. After returning home, Daljeet fell ill, prompting his wife to take him to the hospital.
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: A 29-year-old driver was allegedly beaten to death by a club manager, his wife and three bouncers in north Delhi’s Sarai Rohilla after a party turned violent in the early hours of Sunday.
The man had gone to the club with friends when he allegedly spilled beer on the manager’s wife, who was celebrating her birthday, triggering an argument. Police held five people, including the club manager, his wife and a bouncer, within hours of the incident. The deceased, Daljeet Singh, a resident of JJ Colony in Raghubir Nagar, visited the club on New Rohtak Road in Inderlok in north Delhi around 3.30 am on Oct 11 with five friends, Pawan, Arbaz Ali, Ashu, Tinu and Gautam.
During the altercation, Daljeet and his friends were allegedly assaulted by the club staff. The group later returned to their respective homes in Raghubir Nagar. After reaching home, Daljeet vomited and went to sleep, police said.
His condition deteriorated around noon Sunday, after which his wife, Puja, took him to Guru Gobind Singh Hospital in Khayala, where doctors pronounced him dead. Later, a PCR call was made around 6.52 pm on Sunday.
Police subsequently received information about the death from the hospital and verified the circumstances surrounding the incident. The alleged assault was captured on CCTV cameras.
Five Arrested
How Minor Collision Ended In Murder
Bouncers Attacked Driver For An Hour: Friend
Police have registered an FIR under multiple sections of BNS including for murder, attempt to murder, voluntarily causing hurt, wrongful confinement, and criminal intimidation involving serious threats. Sections under Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act (COTPA) were also included.
The five arrested accused have been identified as Dilawar alias Hasnain, a guest organiser; Sunny alias Gaurav, the club manager; Sharvan Kumar, who was responsible for checking entries at the main gate; bouncer Vikash Balyan; and Harshita, the manager’s wife, whose birthday was being celebrated at the club, according to police. Investigators alleged that Sharvan assaulted Daljeet while another person was taking him back.
Meanwhile, the in charge of Inderlok police post has been sent to District Lines for alleged dereliction of duty after the club was found operating until the early hours of the morning, police said. Sources said the club had remained open until at least 5 am.
Daljeet worked as a driver and was the sole breadwinner for his family, a friend said. He is survived by his wife, an eight-year-old son and a younger brother.
Tinu, one of Daljeet’s friends who was present at the club, said the group had been enjoying themselves when a minor collision caused beer to spill on the manager’s wife.
Another friend alleged that Daljeet was hit on his stomach, legs and head during the assault. This prompted the group to intervene. The situation soon escalated when bouncers joined the altercation, he claimed. He alleged that she grabbed Daljeet by his hair and attacked him with bottles.
“We were seven people and they were more in number. They thrashed us for nearly an hour,” Tinu alleged. He claimed that three members of the group were locked inside a room and beaten for 30 to 40 minutes. The group was allegedly assaulted with sticks and fists. Tinu also alleged that one of the accused pulled out a pistol and threatened them.

briefs.headline: CJP legal head says Delhi Police arrested Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka in Jantar Mantar case
briefs.deck: Delhi Police filed an FIR against Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and other CJP members for allegedly trespassing into the Jantar Mantar area without authorisation
briefs.bodyText:
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das and Ajinkya Shinde have been put under preventive arrest for allegedly entering the Jantar Mantar area without authorisation, officials said on Wednesday (October 14, 2026).
The three were detained early Tuesday (October 13) after they allegedly breached barricades and entered the protest site, which was recently denotified as a designated venue for demonstrations, and raised slogans demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation.
Police have registered a case against them on charges including trespassing, violation of prohibitory orders, breach of a peace bond and obstructing a public servant from discharging official duties, sources said.
Mr. Ranka and Mr. Das had signed a bond to maintain peace for a year after they were detained on Saturday during a previous protest in the national capital, officials said.
The three are likely to be produced before the Special Court of the Executive Magistrate (SEM) later in the morning, sources said.
The arrests come amid heightened security in the national capital following a series of protests by the CJP and other organisations against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
On October 11, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar issued an order designating Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground and CBD Ground as venues for protests and demonstrations, following which Jantar Mantar was denotified as a designated protest site.
The CJP has criticised the move, arguing that shifting demonstrations away from the political centre of the national capital would weaken the visibility of public dissent.

briefs.headline: Response to petitions on illegal detention, clampdown is ready, but needs fine-tuning: Centre
briefs.deck: A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant extended the time for the government to file the reply affidavit by October 15, 2026
briefs.bodyText:
The Union government informed the Supreme Court on Tuesday (October 13, 2026) that its response to petitions alleging illegal detentions, shutdown of public and rail transport, including Metro service, in Delhi on October 10 is “ready” but needs more fine-tuning.
A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant extended the time for the government to file the reply affidavit by October 15.
Multiple petitions, including ones seeking contempt proceedings, were adjourned to October 15, 2026 as one of the judges on the Bench was unwell. The Bench rose for the day shortly thereafter.
Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, for the Centre, said he had gone through the prepared affidavit. It was final, but he wanted to make it “more comprehensive”.
On the petitioners’ request, the Court asked him to share the affidavit, if possible, by October 14, 2026, a day before the hearing so that the lawyers of the petitioners were suitably well-versed with the contents of the affidavit and the hearing would be a meaningful one.
The Court also agreed to urgently hear fresh petitions seeking independent probe and contempt proceedings against authorities on the continued police action against journalists, especially women media professionals, covering the anti-CEC/SIR protests despite an apex court order against it on October 11.
Chief Justice Kant asked the petitioners to cure defects, after which the pleas would also be put up for a comprehensive hearing on Thursday (October 15, 2026). The Court asked for a senior police officer to be present during the next hearing, when allegations of assault on women are raised in the courtroom.
Members of the Supreme Court Bar Association and Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association, of which petitions were adjourned on October 13, gathered at the Supreme Court lawns to express solidarity with the advocates who were assaulted and detained by the police during the October 10 and 11 protests.
A separate petition was orally mentioned by senior advocate Gaurav Bhatia about the “sad” incident which happened in the Supreme Court on October 12, 2026. Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and other Opposition leaders had come to the Supreme Court Registry after filing a petition seeking a probe into SIR and allegations of arbitrary functioning and misconduct against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Mr. Gandhi’s arrival had drawn a crowd of lawyers around the Registry block within the Supreme Court premises, and the participants of his ‘March for Democracy’ converged in large numbers at the outer gates of the court.
Mr. Bhatia said a petition filed by advocate Divyansh Bisht has sought initiation of criminal contempt against Mr. Gandhi and other Opposition leaders for obstructing justice, a ban on political demonstrations inside court premises, a “neutral framework” to regulate protests near courts, and safeguards against political interference in sub judice cases.
The court also saw the urgent mentioning of petitions filed by organisations of media professionals, including Free Speech Collective and Network of Women in Media, India, which said the violence visited upon journalists, both on October 10, 2026 and October 11, 2026, were “not merely isolated obstruction, but an asserted course of police action comprising unlawful detention, forcible removal, physical assault, manhandling, intimidation, disregard of press credentials and the calculated exclusion and removal of journalists from places where public power was being exercised”.
The petition, filed through Aarthi Rajan, said “unless restrained by law and judicial review, such conduct converts the constitutional freedom of the press into a paper guarantee”.
Network of Women in Media, India, said the “physical handling, intimidation, forcible removal and detention of women journalists in particular interferes not only with newsgathering and freedom of the press, but also with their dignity, bodily integrity, personal liberty and equal ability to participate in the profession”.
“A free press must be able to approach, observe, question, record and report the exercise of public power, especially during protests, dispersals, arrests and crowdcontrol operations. If the police may equate observation with participation, disregard credentials, seize the reporter’s person and remove the reporter from the scene, the resulting account is necessarily filtered by the very authority whose conduct requires independent scrutiny. The chilling effect is immediate: journalists retreat, evidence disappears, public knowledge contracts and democratic accountability is defeated,” the petitions submitted.
Senior advocate Nitya Ramakrishnan said that “documentary proof of students being abused in police stations” have been placed on record before the Supreme Court and should also be taken up for hearing on October 15, 2026.
Another petition filed by a Supreme Court advocate group, Lawyers’ Association for Constitution, along with advocates Fidel Tom and Sumita Hazarika, has alleged that the police were brutal with people who they had detained. Mr. Tom said he was assaulted inside the police station.
The petition, filed through advocate Subhash Chandran, alleged that detention of women after 6 p.m. without any report or permission was in clear violation of their fundamental rights to dignity.
It sought a complete list of persons detained or arrested on October 10 and 11 with the time, place and ground of detention, the officers responsible, the places of custody, the time of release, whether the arrest memo, grounds of arrest and information to a relative were given, and whether production before a Magistrate or release was effected within the statutory time.

briefs.headline: US State Secretary Marco Rubio to travel to Uzbekistan, India from Oct 17-22; visit to Jamnagar on cards
briefs.bodyText: Washington: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will travel to India next week to further strengthen energy cooperation, the Department of State said on Tuesday. . Rubio will first visit Samarkand in Uzbekistan, and will then travel to Mumbai and Jamnagar in India from October 17-22, it said. . This will be Rubio’s second visit to India since May, when he attended the Quad Foreign Ministers’ meeting hosted by External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar in New Delhi. . “He will meet with senior government officials to strengthen the US-India strategic partnership, exchange views on regional and global dynamics, and discuss prospects for enhanced energy cooperation,” the State Department said. .EAM S Jaishankar reiterates India's concerns over Russia sanctions Act to Marco Rubio. Rubio will also meet with business leaders to promote opportunities for commercial investment and economic cooperation, it said. . Rubio’s visit to Jamnagar is crucial as it is home to Reliance’s refinery, the world’s largest single-site facility with a capacity to process 1.4 million barrels per day of crude oil. . In March, President Donald Trump announced that the US will build its first refinery in 50 years with investment from Reliance Industries. . The refinery will come up at Brownsville in Texas at a cost of $300 billion, Trump said. . In Samarkand, Rubio will participate in the C5+1 Ministerial to highlight how strategic cooperation through this diplomatic platform promotes a more peaceful and prosperous future for the United States and the countries of Central Asia. . The Secretary will also participate in bilateral engagements with senior officials from all C5 countries -- Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and the Kyrgyz Republic. . A US commercial delegation comprising over 200 business leaders will accompany Rubio, ushering in a new era of strengthened commercial cooperation for the United States and Central Asia.

briefs.headline: EPFO extends ECR filing due date to October 31
briefs.deck: EPFO extends ECR filing due date to Oct 31
briefs.bodyText: Bengaluru: The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has extended the due date for filing the Electronic Challan-cum-Return (ECR) and remitting statutory contributions for the September 2026 wage month to October 31, 2026. The earlier deadline was October 15. . In a circular issued on Tuesday, PB Verman, Additional Central Provident Fund Commissioner (Compliance), said with approval of the Central Provident Fund Commissioner (CPFC), the extension has been announced. It was issued using powers under the second proviso to paragraph 28(3) of the Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme, 1952. The relief follows a revision of the wage ceiling limit, effective September 17, 2026. Establishments covered under the Code on Social Security, 2020, and its Schemes have had to change their payroll systems and compliance processes to correctly compute wages and provident fund and allied contributions. .EPFO wage ceiling raised to Rs 25,000 to cover 51 lakh more workers. According to EPFO, it received multiple representations from employers, establishments and other stakeholders. They said the mid-month change forced modifications to pay-bills, payroll configurations and employee-wise contribution calculations, creating technical, operational and administrative difficulties in preparing and submitting the ECR for September.

briefs.headline: Average passenger vehicle loan amount rose 49% in 7 years: Report
briefs.deck: 'Average PV loan amount up 49% in 7 yrs'
briefs.bodyText: Bengaluru: India’s average passenger vehicle loan amount rose 49% to Rs 8.2 lakh in H1 2026 from H1 2019, according to TransUnion CIBIL’s Shifting Gears 2026 report. . Average repayment tenure increased by five months to 62 months over the same period. . The report attributed the rise to preferences for SUVs and feature-rich vehicles, alongside higher vehicle prices. Financing has become more central to car ownership as consumers opt for higher-value purchases. .Passenger vehicle dispatches clock Q1 record of 12,73,811 units in FY27: SIAM. Bhavesh Jain, MD and CEO, TransUnion CIBIL, said, “A first-time car buyer, someone moving up from a two-wheeler, a repeat buyer and a customer upgrading to a higher-value vehicle can have very different credit histories and financial profiles. Credit information can bring greater clarity to these journeys and support more informed and responsible financing decisions.” . Semi-urban and rural borrowers accounted for 51% of consumers taking another higher-value car loan in H1 2026, up six percentage points from 2019. . NBFCs accounted for 73% of two-wheeler loans and 37% of passenger vehicle loans. . The active passenger vehicle borrower base reached 2.5 crore in June 2026, 1.7 times the June 2019 level.

stories.headline: SC/ST voices condemn Karnataka Hight Court verdict striking down enhanced reservation
stories.deck: Various individuals and organisations representing Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes communities in the State expressed deep disappointment with the Karnataka High Court verdict that struck down the enhanced reservation
stories.bodyText:
Various individuals and organisations representing Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes communities in the State expressed deep disappointment with the Karnataka High Court verdict that struck down the enhanced reservation.
Basavaraj Kowthal, convener of Forum for Justice for Scheduled Castes, criticised that it is unfair to sacrifice the share of SC/ST communities in reservation to maintain a 50% ceiling. “Because of political equations, OBCs have been given 32%. It could be reduced to 27% and the SC/ST share could be increased to 24%,” he suggested.
The Karnataka Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Reservation of Seats in Educational Institutions and of Appointments or Posts in the Services under the State) Act, 2022, was introduced by the Basavaraj Bommai-led BJP government in the State in 2023. However, the law was not added by the Central Government to the Ninth Schedule, which would have provided it some shielding from being challenged in courts.
“The BJP took pride in its double-engine sarkar, and the Union government brought in the constitutional amendment providing 10% EWS reservation. Why, then, did they not do this? It shows how anti-Dalit they are,” Mr. Kowthal criticised.
He also criticised the Congress government, saying that while previous Chief Minister Siddaramaiah had written to the Union government seeking the inclusion of the law in the Ninth Schedule, the government should have exerted more pressure on the Union government.
Grave injustice
V.S. Ugrappa, former MP and Congress leader, pointed out that the 2011 Census puts the SC population in Karnataka at around 17.1% and the ST population at 7%. “Both the reports of Justice Nagmohan Das and Justice Subhash B. Adi have indicated that SCs, STs and OBCs are inadequately represented in employment and education. None of these aspects has been considered by the court,” he said.
“There are only two possible remedies for a permanent solution. First, the law must be included in the Ninth Schedule, as was done in Tamil Nadu. Second, the Karnataka government must challenge the order by filing a special leave petition before the Supreme Court,” he said.
Joint effort
D. Chandraiah from The Karnataka State SC/ST Employees’ Association said that legal experts, senior advocates, and the government are being consulted to ensure that a unified, strong legal challenge is mounted in the Supreme Court against the HC verdict.
According to him, the association will implead itself as a party/litigant in the Supreme Court proceedings. The association will also submit a joint memorandum on Thursday to the Cabinet Sub-Committee on backlog vacancies.
“The 10% EWS did not violate the 50% cap, but adding a 6% hike for SC and ST was deemed a violation by the court. This is inconsistent,” he said.
Mr. Chandraiah criticised the government for failing to convince the High Court using available empirical data regarding the backwardness of SC/ST communities across key sectors, including education, healthcare, land ownership, industry, commerce, and so on. He added that the court also failed to adequately consider whether the report findings constituted the “extraordinary circumstances” under which reservation could exceed 50%.

stories.headline: FIR on IAS officer for attack on police at Bengaluru nightclub
stories.deck: An IAS officer, Vikas Marmat, and his associates were booked for attacking police at a nightclub. The incident occurred when police checked for underage drinking on October 9. Vikas reacted angrily when asked for identification from young women present. After confronting police officers, the group was taken to a local police station. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Nara Chandrababu Naidu has…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: An Andhra Pradesh-cadre IAS officer and his realtor-friend were among the four booked on charges of abusing and attacking police officers at a nightclub on Residency Road in Bengaluru when the latter were checking the credentials of customers to ensure liquor was not served to underage customers.
The 2019-batch officer under police scanner is Vikas Marmat, currently serving as project director of Kuppam Area Development Authority in AP chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu’s home constituency, Kuppam. His friends booked are Abhay Uday Singh, a real estate businessman and resident of Akshaynagar on Bannerghatta Road, and Nitish, owner of a competitive exams coaching centre and resident of Bihar. The fourth person booked is Roshan, a bouncer.
While the officer has been named as primary accused, others were named co-accused in the incident that took place on the night of Oct 9. Next morning, Vikas and others apologised for their act, police said.
The incident unfolded when sleuths from Central Crime Branch (CCB) visited Cavore on Residency Road as part of a drive to check underage revelry at liquor joints. A team led by inspector Arun Salunke visited the outlet around 1.30am. 
While interacting with revellers, a police officer asked a few young women to produce documents to prove age. This made Vikas and Abhay angry. They allegedly started behaving tersely with the police.
“First, Vikas, saying he was an IAS officer, asked what rights we had to ask the girls to produce age documents. We replied stating this was part of a special drive against pubs and bars that serve liquor to minors. Then, Vikas asked under whose direction we were doing it. We replied that our police commissioner has directed it. Then, Vikas asked what’s our jurisdiction limit. We replied CCB covers the entire city. At this, Vikas became furious, saying no such powers have been given to police, where one branch can act anywhere in the city like Bengaluru. By then, he abused us. When we resisted, Abhay Uday Singh pushed and attacked us,” a cop present at the scene told TOI.
Nitish and Roshan too allegedly abused and pushed other cops, asking them to go out. Vikas allegedly hurled expletives at the cops, which was videographed and the same went viral on Tuesday. Soon, more police force reached the place and all four men were taken to Cubbon Park police station.
Police inspector Arun Salunke registered the FIR stating the four allegedly picked up an altercation, abused and attacked the cops on duty. Accordingly, police registered a case against Vikas, Abhay, Nitish and Roshan for criminal intimidation, assault on a public servant to prevent them from discharging their duties and use of criminal force to dishonour a person.
CM Naidu orders probe
Following demands by YSRCP, Andhra Pradesh chief minister Nara Chandrababu Naidu has directed the chief secretary to submit a detailed report on the incident. The CM’s office is said to have taken serious note of the incident and is reportedly reviewing the matter for potential disciplinary action.

stories.headline: Amid AI push, no internet in 48% of K’taka schools
stories.deck: Despite IT Capital Tag, Karnataka Fares Worst In South India In School Internet Access
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: While 
Karnataka
 is favouring introduction of AI skills and coding in its schools, nearly 48% of the state’s 74,578 schools do not have internet connectivity, exposing a glaring digital divide.
According to UDISE+ report released by Union ministry of education for 2025–26, the state’s connectivity rate is well below the national average of 67%. Nearly one in three schools in India lacks internet access, while every second school in Karnataka lacks the facility.
Home to the country’s IT capital, Karnataka has the highest percentage of schools without internet connectivity among the southern states — both as a proportion of total schools and in absolute numbers.
The gap is particularly alarming in government schools. Of the state’s 48,527 government-managed schools, only 18,007 have internet facilities, leaving about 30,520 (63%) without connectivity.
These contrasting figures come at a time when chief minister 
DK Shivakumar
, during his Independence Day, announced the AI Akshara Abhiyana and Coding Gurukula initiatives across Karnataka, aimed at introducing AI education in schools from Class 6.
Subsequently, the CM said AI training had already begun for Class 9 students in govt schools and directed officials to explore extending it to younger students, with support from the information technology department and private organisations. However, the widening infrastructure gap raises questions about how uniformly these initiatives can be implemented across the state.
D Shashi Kumar, general secretary of the Associated Managements of Primary and Secondary Schools in Karnataka (KAMS), pointed out that the digital divide could widen if the number of schools with functional internet connections were considered, as several schools reporting internet access do not have an active connection.
“AI education requires access to computers, suitable software, trained teachers and, for many learning applications, reliable internet connectivity. Without these basic facilities, students in poorly connected schools risk being left behind even as their peers gain exposure to emerging technologies. Although the government has pinned its hopes on CSR initiatives, how many schools will these initiatives cover? All these programmes require substantial financial resources. Will the government be able to provide the necessary funds?” he asked.
Karnataka’s performance is also poor compared with that of its southern neighbours. Andhra Pradesh has internet access in 99.2% of its 60,843 schools, while Tamil Nadu has achieved 99% coverage across 57,566 schools. Kerala reports connectivity in 92.6% of its 15,750 schools. Telangana, despite having a sizeable gap of its own, has internet access in 76.5% of its 41,762 schools. Karnataka, with connectivity in just 51.7% of its schools, has the lowest coverage in South India, the report revealed.
“The proportion of schools without internet connectivity in Karnataka is more than twice that of Telangana, where 23.5% of schools lack access, and over six times the national average of 32.6%,” a Bengaluru-based academician said.
Nationally, 4.77 lakh of India’s 14.67 lakh schools lack internet access, according to the report. Karnataka accounts for approximately 7.5% of the nationwide deficit.

stories.headline: Bengaluru court restrains media, tech platforms from disseminating defamatory vidoes on Siddaramaiah
stories.bodyText:
A Bengaluru civil court on Tuesday issued an ad-interim ex-parte temporary injunction restraining further circulation of two videos telecast on two private YouTube channels making allegedly defamatory remarks against former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah.
The interim order restrains 42 media houses, including newspapers, television channels, digital platforms like YouTube, Yahoo, Google and Facebook, from disseminating the impugned videos, their captions, clips, extracts, or substantially identical versions through any medium.
B. Pushpanjali, judge of the 19th additional city civil and sessions court, Bengaluru, passed the interim order on a suit filed by Mr. Siddaramaiah.
Additionally, the court directed YouTube, Yahoo, Google and Facebook, to forthwith disable access to and block the specified URLs of the two videos telecast on the YouTube channels on September 27, 2026, with title “Karnataka Honey Trap Nexus Part-1”, and October 2, 2026 with the title “Live: Biggest CD Blast in Karnataka Politics?”.
In the suit, Mr. Siddaramaiah categorically denied all the allegations made in the two videos. In one of the videos, a woman narrates a 2011 incident, allegedly when she was 14 and links it to him in a conversation with two men, “the recording of which was in a manner intended to resemble a clandestine or hidden-camera recording,” it has been stated in the suit.
The caption, it further says, “is deliberately framed to place the plaintiff at the centre of a sensational political and sexual narrative,” sans any material.
It has been pointed out in the suit that the caption to the video links the alleged recording of conversation as a reason for him to demit the office of Chief Minister, alleged blackmail, an alleged honey-trap network, the present Chief Minister, statements of other political leaders, the Congress High Command, and Leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi.
“...The attempt to retrospectively connect a political transition with an alleged secretly recorded conversation is false, baseless and designed to injure Mr. Siddaramaiah’s reputation and political standing,” it has been claimed in the suit.
Since Mr. Siddaramaiah has challenged the authenticity, credibility, intent of the videos, the court observed that permitting their circulation at this stage could seriously harm his dignity, reputation and privacy. It noted that if media houses are not restrained from broadcasting or sharing the videos or their clips, the resulting damage would be irreparable.

briefs.headline: Can’t fight a war with 95% indigenous systems if critical 5% is imported, says DRDO in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 India cannot effectively fight future wars with defence systems that are 95% indigenous if the remaining 5% consists of critical imported technologies such as chips, software or algorithms, BK Das, Director General (Electronics & Communication Systems), 
DRDO
, said Tuesday, in Bengaluru.
Addressing a curtain-raiser event in Bengaluru ahead of the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC)-2026, Das stressed that the country must pursue “last-mile indigenisation” to achieve true technological self-reliance in defence and strategic sectors. “You can’t fight a war with a 95% indigenous system where the critical 5% does not exist,” Das said, arguing that even a small imported component could determine the effectiveness of an entire weapon system during conflict.
The remarks come as DRDO prepares to lead a thematic session on “Semiconductors and Next-Gen Chips” at ESTIC-2026, which will be held at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi from Oct 27 to 29. The national conclave, being organised under the guidance of the principal scientific adviser to the govt of India, is expected to bring together policymakers, industry leaders, researchers and academia to deliberate on emerging technologies and India’s innovation roadmap.
Highlighting the strategic importance of semiconductors, Das said the future of warfare and advanced defence systems would increasingly be determined by technologies embedded at the chip level. “The last square inch of silicon is going to decide the future of warfare,” he said, urging Indian researchers, start-ups, academia and industries to focus on indigenous chip design and next-generation semiconductor technologies.
Das said India had made significant progress in defence self-reliance over the past two decades, moving from being one of the world’s largest importers of defence equipment to developing and deploying indigenous systems. However, he cautioned that complete technological sovereignty would only be achieved when critical technologies are designed, developed and manufactured within the country.

briefs.headline: Gombe Habba: Elaborate themes take over a year of prep in Bengaluru households
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: A doll sitting upright may not be enough for Bengaluru’s Gombe Habba enthusiasts anymore. As elaborate themes become central to annual displays, some families are making and customising dolls to fit the stories they want to tell.
The preparations do not just begin a week or a month before. The plans for next year’s 
Dasara
 begin the previous year itself. In Girinagar, a mother-in-law and daughter-in-law duo have spent the past year preparing a 
Ramayana
-themed display. “After visiting Ayodhya, we decided to arrange our dolls along the Ramayana theme this year. We are planning to keep around 600 dolls and we have made around 10% of them by hand this year. We have made wire dolls, which are easier to make in any pose and posture,” said Maduri Anandh, the daughter-in-law who works as an admin officer for a private company.
The family has been arranging Gombe Habba dolls for 12-13 years, with their collection now including dolls from the UK, US, Japan and Australia. During the 10-day festival, the display occupies almost the entire house.
For Rajajinagar resident Padma B Udayakumar, too, the work begins much earlier than the festival. The 52-year-old has been arranging dolls for over four decades and has won several national and international Gombe Habba contests. 
This year, she is recreating the sanctum sanctorum of Tirumala in Tirupati and Andal Vaibhavam, celebrating Srivaishnavism. “Andal is one of the saint poetesses,” Padma said.
For Padma, the display is also an exercise in documentation. “This has become my identity now, with visitors expecting creativity out of me every year. I even keep my research material in a printed form so that those who come to see the dolls also get to read it,” she said.
Padma began giving her displays a specific theme after the pandemic. Her earlier themes have included Indian textiles, ancient Indian games and Navadurga puja.

briefs.headline: ‘Dissent not a crime’: Bengaluru lawyers demand probe by Centre
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Condemning police action against their colleagues and students during anti-SIR protests in Delhi and Bengaluru in the past four days, dozens of lawyers Tuesday demanded apology from the Union govt for unlawful detentions, while welcoming 
Karnataka chief minister
’s order to probe the Bengaluru incident.
Unlike the chaos on Monday when protesting lawyers were manhandled allegedly near KR Circle, Tuesday’s demonstrations by Indian Association of Lawyers and All Indian Lawyers Association for Justice in front of the city civil court remained peaceful. Despite protesting outside the designated site of Freedom Park, police officers did not attempt to detain or remove the peaceful protesters.
‘Batons cannot silence the constitution’ and ‘dissent is not a crime’ were some of the placards on display during protest.
On the CM’s probe order, Clifton D’Rozario, AILAJ’s general secretary, said, “This is the difference between a party that believes in democracy and others who don’t. The state govt immediately said they’ll look into it. I’m sure they’ll take action.”
Clifton was among the advocates allegedly manhandled by police Monday. “Police are always in favour of the ruling class,” he added.
The lawyers sought resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged discrepancies in the special intensive revision process.
“Today’s protest by lawyers in Bengaluru is due to several issues: SIR, manhandling of lawyers, and we’re looking for the rule of the law. When we are supposed to uphold the rule of law, we are treated like this,” said Shilpa Prasad, a lawyer.
Avani Choksi, an advocate focused on labour law, said the protest was planned well before Monday chaos with a larger focus on Delhi. They hinted at more protests if the Union govt does not act early.

briefs.headline: March blocked, but anti-SIR activists vow to continue fight in Bengaluru
briefs.deck: Memorandum To CEO Emailed | Groups Want Electoral Rolls As Of Jan 2025 Restored
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 The protesters detained Monday while attempting to march to the Chief Electoral Officer’s (CEO) office to submit a memorandum opposing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Karnataka have submitted the memorandum by email and vowed to continue their agitation.
The memorandum, prepared by My Vote, My Right — a coalition of over 40 civil society organisations, including trade unions, women’s groups and human rights organisations, along with other democratic rights groups and citizens — demands the cancellation of the SIR process in Karnataka, restoration of electoral rolls as they stood in Jan 2025, and the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
“There’s no question of backing out. The issue is serious. While we’ve already written to the Karnataka home minister about the way police acted on Monday, there’s another question that remains unanswered,” said Clifton Rozario, national general secretary of All India Lawyers Association for Justice, who was allegedly assaulted during the protest. “I’ve been at many protests over the years, and Monday’s police behaviour was unfamiliar, to say the least. So, the question we have is: has the election commission communicated something to the police that has not been made public?” Rozario asked
.
A key concern raised in the memorandum is the deletion of eligible voters’ names from electoral rolls. Claiming that more than one crore names have been deleted from Karnataka’s rolls, the signatories said street vendors, migrant workers, single women, members of the LGBTQIA+ community, Dalits and religious minorities were among the worst affected.
Bengalureans continued to gather at Freedom Park Tuesday to oppose SIR and condemn the detention of activists in the country
The memorandum also highlights the low rate of reinstatement of deleted names through Form 6, the application used to seek inclusion in electoral rolls. According to the signatories, eligible voters are facing difficulties in getting their names restored even through this mechanism, raising concerns about their ability to exercise their right to vote.
The memorandum warns that marginalised communities face a disproportionate risk of exclusion because of difficulties in producing documents, migration, discrepancies in name, and arbitrary objections. “Excluding these groups would deepen existing inequalities in democratic representation,” said Vinay Sreenivasa of My Vote, My Right.
The signatories also expressed concern over the alleged misuse of Form 7, which allows objections to be filed against the inclusion of names in electoral rolls. They claimed that the process had created opportunities for politically motivated deletions, particularly targeting Muslims and Dalits.
According to the memorandum, concerns over large-scale deletions, procedural irregularities, lack of transparency and inadequate accountability have eroded public confidence in the SIR process. It calls for safeguards against arbitrary deletions and the misuse of the objection mechanism in future electoral roll revisions. “Along with scrapping the ongoing SIR and restoring the Jan 2025 rolls, we’ve urged that future revisions be conducted through a transparent, lawful and publicly accountable process, ensuring that no eligible voter is deprived of the right to vote,” Sreenivasa said.

briefs.headline: SIR in Karnataka: Booth-level officers shift focus to voter roll changes ahead of Oct 22 deadline
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 With notices and hearings nearing completion, booth-level officers (BLOs) have shifted their focus to processing applications for voter addition, deletion and correction submitted before the Sept 23 deadline through Forms 6, 7 and 8. The electoral machinery has until Oct 22 to dispose of pending claims and objections.
Form 6 is used to apply for inclusion in the electoral roll, Form 7 to seek deletion of a name, and Form 8 to update voter details, shift registration to another address, or replace an elector photo identity card (EPIC).
An official from the chief electoral officer’s office said most of the nearly 19.5 lakh applications have been processed, with the remaining forms expected to be cleared by the end of the week.
A BLO supervisor in Mahadevapura said physical verification of applicants under Forms 6 and 8 had begun alongside house-to-house verification of documents submitted by voters served notices.
Although no Form 7 application had been received at his booth, applications under Form 8 to shift voter registration to Mahadevapura would automatically generate a Form 7 request to delete the voter’s name from the previous address.
Karnataka
 has received 58,220 Form 7 applications, around 80% of which are generated through Form 8 applications when voters shift their registration, a senior official said.
Assistant electoral registration officers in Bengaluru Central said BLOs had also begun processing Forms 6 and 8 even as the notice and hearing process continued.
Meanwhile, the deputy commissioners of Bidar and Vijayapura told 
TOI

briefs.headline: Why can’t Bengaluru protest outside Freedom Park?
briefs.deck: An HC order and a police licensing regime have made Freedom Park the city’s default protest venue. But the governing police order also gives the police commissioner discretion to designate another suitable venue, meaning the legal position is more nuanced than an absolute ban on demonstrations elsewhere
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru has largely confined protests to Freedom Park for years. The practice stems from a suo motu case initiated in Karnataka high court in 2021 over the impact of demonstrations on traffic and the rights of non-participants.
How did restriction begin?
On March 3, 2022, a division bench of HC passed an interim order directing the state govt to ensure that protests, processions and similar activities were held only at Freedom Park, Gandhinagar, and nowhere else in Bengaluru. The court also directed that such activities be organised without adversely affecting traffic, particularly during rush hours, and that action be taken wherever traffic was disrupted.
On Aug 1, 2022, HC disposed of the case. Paragraph 4 recorded a submission that protests, marches and dharnas would be permitted only at Freedom Park, and that the state was obliged to enforce the 2021 licensing order. Paragraph 5 directed the authorities to ensure compliance with that order “in letter and spirit” and to continue taking action against violators.
What does police order say?
The Licensing and Regulation of Protests, Demonstrations and Protest Marches (Bengaluru City) Order, 2021, published in the state gazette in Jan 2022, currently governs protests in the city. 
It stipulates that protests, demonstrations, dharnas and protest marches cannot be held in the city without a licence under the order.
Clause 4.1 identifies Freedom Park as the designated venue for protests in Bengaluru. However, it also empowers the police commissioner to designate another suitable location in the city, depending on the situation. The licensing authority may determine the number of participants permitted at Freedom Park based on the nature and duration of the programme and the venue’s capacity.
Are protests outside Freedom Park illegal?
Not necessarily in every circumstance. The 2021 order does not expressly prohibit protest marches or designate Freedom Park as the only possible venue. Instead, it identifies Freedom Park while retaining the police commissioner’s discretion to designate another suitable location.
A legal backgrounder prepared by activists argues that the HC’s final order did not direct that protests be held exclusively at Freedom Park, but required compliance with the licensing order. According to this interpretation, the judgment neither bars rallies nor mandates Freedom Park as the sole venue.
The distinction is important: the March 2022 interim order expressly restricted protests and processions to Freedom Park, while the Aug 2022 final order required enforcement of the 2021 licensing rules. Both orders must be read alongside the licensing order before arriving at a definitive legal conclusion.
Why does this matter?
Activists argue that restricting demonstrations to a single venue reduces their visibility and makes it harder for groups to draw public attention to local grievances. The backgrounder says the restrictions have affected workers, farmers, Dalit activists, sanitation workers and residents seeking to protest over issues in their own localities.
The debate centres on balancing traffic management and public convenience with the constitutional right to assemble peacefully and express dissent. For now, Freedom Park remains Bengaluru’s designated dominant protest venue. Whether, and under what conditions, the police commissioner exercises the discretion to permit demonstrations elsewhere remains central to the controversy.

briefs.headline: Karnataka to explore legal options to challenge High Court verdict striking down reservation enhancement
briefs.deck: Congress leaders question hurried introduction of law by the previous BJP government before the Assembly elections in 2023, Veerashaiva Mahasabha welcomes the ruling
briefs.bodyText:
Following the Karnataka High Court striking down the enhancement of reservation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the State, Congress leaders said the government is exploring legal options to challenge the order and safeguard ongoing recruitment and education admissions. The leaders have also questioned the Union government’s reluctance to include the law in the Ninth Schedule.
Cabinet to discuss
Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara said the High Court verdict will be discussed comprehensively by the Cabinet, following which a decision will be taken on the future course of action, including the possibility of filing an appeal in the Supreme Court.
Speaking to media representatives, he said that if a situation arises in which the overall reservation percentage has to be reduced, the percentages under internal reservation may also have to be revised proportionately. While mathematically, such a revision may not be difficult, the more serious concern is that it could reduce the opportunities available to different communities, he said.
The matter is expected to be discussed in the Cabinet on Thursday as per government sources.
Abrupt implementation
In a statement issued following the Karnataka High Court judgment that struck down the increase in reservation — from 15% to 17% for SCs, and from 3% to 7% for STs – the Deputy Chief Minister stated that the “verdict highlights the irresponsibility of the previous BJP government and the persistent neglect of the BJP-led Union government.”
“Why did the previous BJP government abruptly implement the reservation increase law just before the 2023 Assembly elections without laying a proper Constitutional foundation? In October 2022 itself, the then BJP government was fully aware that increasing the SC/ST reservation would raise Karnataka’s total quota to 56%, thereby breaching the prevailing 50% ceiling,” he said.
Pointing to the Union government’s reply in Parliament on July 25, 2026, stating that the proposal to include Karnataka’s reservation Act in the Ninth Schedule was deferred because the matter was sub-judice, the Deputy Chief Minister termed it unacceptable.
Exceptional circumstances
Expressing his personal view on the High Court verdict, Mr. Parameshwara said that Karnataka’s circumstances could have been examined as an exceptional case.
“Tamil Nadu has been provided 69% reservation through a Constitutional amendment. When such an arrangement has been made there, the additional 6% reservation beyond the 50% ceiling in Karnataka could also have been examined as a special case in light of its social circumstances,” he said.
‘Explain constitutional solution’
Former Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah too questioned the BJP’s move to announce enhanced reservation without first ensuring its Constitutional sustainability.
“The BJP-led Union government subsequently deferred Karnataka’s request for inclusion in the Ninth Schedule, citing pending litigation. It must now explain what constitutional solution it proposes,” he said.
Noting that the Justice Nagamohan Das Committee, constituted during the Congress government, had provided the foundation for enhancing reservation, Mr. Siddaramaiah demanded that the Union government review the 50% ceiling, facilitate a constitutionally sustainable framework for population-informed reservation, and reconsider Karnataka’s Ninth Schedule proposal.
Accusing the BJP of ‘muddying the waters’, Home Minister Priyank Kharge said, “I’m hearing that one of the observations by the court is that it was not done through a consultative process. It sems like the BJP government hurried it for electoral gains. The 50% ceiling is already breached through EWS. And there are states like Tamil Nadu with 69% reservation. So how is that constitutional and this unconstitutional?”
Mahasabha welcomes verdict
Meanwhile, H.M. Renuka Prasanna, national secretary for the All India Veerashaiva Mahasabha, welcomed the verdict, terming it “a good example that nobody is above the Constitution.”
“The issue has been dragging on in court for the last four years, and with no relaxation in the age limit for jobs, many were deprived of the opportunity,” he said.
Stressing that the organisation is not against the SC/ST community, he added, “Our argument is simply that if the government had abided by the SC verdict not to breach the 50% ceiling, then so many people wouldn’t be left waiting.”

briefs.headline: Four arrested for forcing 13 children to beg in Bengaluru
briefs.deck: Children rescued near Kogilu Cross, Yelahanka; handed over to Child Welfare Committee
briefs.bodyText:
Four persons from other States have been taken into custody for allegedly engaging children in begging at traffic signals across Bengaluru, following a joint operation by the Central Crime Branch (CCB) Women Protection Wing and the Social Welfare Department. 13 children were rescued during the operation.
Among the 13 children were toddlers and teenagers, police sources said. Some of them may have been rented out by their own parents to beg, the police suspect.
Acting on credible information, the police conducted a raid on makeshift huts erected on the footpath beneath the flyover near Kogilu Cross on Monday. The information indicated that persons from other States were staying there and allegedly using children for begging.
During the operation, the police detained four persons and questioned them. According to the police, the four admitted during interrogation that they had kept the children with them and had made them beg at traffic signals across Bengaluru to earn money.
The four accused were subsequently handed over to the Yelahanka police. The 13 rescued children were produced before the Child Welfare Committee, along with a report, for further action, including efforts to trace their biological parents.
The operation was carried out as part of efforts to prevent the exploitation of children and identify those allegedly forcing minors to beg for money.
Further legal action is expected following the police investigation and the Child Welfare Committee’s intervention.

stories.headline: Rollout of BS-VII in 3 phases from April 2029 to April 2035
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Govt is all set to roll out BS-VII emission standards, aligned with Euro 7 norms, in phases, starting April 2029. The new norms will set stricter limits on harmful pollutants, including nitrogen oxides, hydrocarbons and particulate matter amid heightened pollution risks across Indian cities.
BS-VII will start with new cars and SUVs manufactured from April 2029, followed by small goods delivery and pick-up vans from 2030 and buses and heavy-duty vehicles from April 2031. The new norms for two-wheelers - the biggest contributor to pollution - will, however, be notified later.
Unlike BS-VI, which was first rolled out from April 2020, it will not require changes in the refinery infrastructure to produce petrol and diesel suitable for the upgraded emission standards, officials said. It will, however, require the automobile sector to upgrade engines.
TOI has learnt that the road transport ministry has approved the proposed timeline, and draft notifications for the three categories of vehicles are expected over the next few days. The proposed emission norms will not affect existing vehicles or their life, including those compliant with BS-VI standards.
The proposed standards will strengthen emissions monitoring beyond controlled laboratory tests to ensure vehicles comply with prescribed limits under real-world driving conditions and throughout their operational life. 
The implementation of all the new norms will be in three phases spanning six years - April 2029 to April 2035 - giving adequate time to industry and testing agencies.
According to the finalised norms, the cut-off limits of various emission components for cars and SUVs remain unchanged compared with BS-VI. Particulate number has, however, been reduced fr-om 23 nanometres to 10 nanometres, resulting in improved filtration of pollutants. Smaller particles penetrate deeper into lungs. A person aware of the matter said the proposed change makes the regulation more stringent by capturing ultrafine particles, which have been unregulated thus far.
The transition from BS-VI to BS-VII will have more impact on trucks and heavy-duty vehicles, with the proposed standard aimed at reducing emissions in the range of 20-50% across pollutants. This will be more stringent for on-road emissions.
People involved in framing the norms said BS-VII goes beyond tailpipe emission by regulating non-exhaust sources such as brake wear and tyre abrasion. Moreover, the new norms will introduce the concept of market surveillance, where independent testing agencies will conduct in-use compliance checks.
Officials said the norms are fully aligned with Euro 7 and its implementation, which was also structured in a phased manner, starting Nov 2026 for light-duty vehicles and May 2028 for heavy-duty vehicles. The full rollout will extend up to 2035.

stories.headline: Apple makes fresh push into smart homes market
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Apple is making a renewed push into the smart home market, unveiling three new devices - HomeView, HomePod mini 2 and Apple TV 4K - as it looks to take its newly launched Siri AI beyond smartphones and establish a stronger presence in connected homes. The launches mark Apple's latest attempt to challenge Amazon and Google in a market where it has struggled to gain significant traction despite its strong presence in premium consumer electronics.
The centrepiece of the announcement is HomeView, a smart home display that acts as a central hub for controlling connected devices, managing household activities and interacting with Siri AI. The device is priced at Rs 39,900.
Apple also introduced the second-generation HomePod mini at Rs 18,900 and a refreshed Apple TV 4K, starting at Rs 39,900. The new devices will become available in phases, beginning Oct 30.
"Apple must demonstrate that context-aware AI makes the connected home meaningfully more useful, while addressing interoperability and adoption barriers," said Prabhu Ram, VP, industry research group, CyberMedia Research (CMR).

stories.headline: Warner Music bets high on regional talent, technology, diversified revenue streams in India: Jay Mehta
stories.deck: The music company is looking to deepen its presence in regional markets, expand artist services, and use its global network to take Indian music to international audiences
stories.bodyText:
India’s music industry is entering a new phase of growth, driven by the rise of regional and non-film music, expanding digital consumption, and the growing role of technology in artist discovery and audience development, said Jay Mehta, Managing Director, Recorded Music and Publishing, India & SAARC, Warner Music Group (WMG), a Manhattan-based music and entertainment conglomerate and one of the Big Three in the global music industry alongside Universal Music Group and Sony Music Entertainment
Warner Music India, the Indian arm of WMG, is positioning itself to capitalise on these changes by moving beyond the conventional record-label model and building a broader music and entertainment business spanning recorded music, publishing, distribution, artist services, live entertainment, and strategic partnerships.
“India needs to be approached as a multi-market music ecosystem rather than a single market,’’ Mr. Mehta told The Hindu in an exclusive conversation, pointing to the company’s focus on artists with strong cultural connections to their audiences, from established names such as Guru Randhawa and Darshan Raval to emerging regional performers.
Its original intellectual property, Maati (an indigenous folk music record label and franchise by WMI), brings together music and artists across Indian languages and cultures, creating opportunities for discovery beyond traditional linguistic and genre boundaries. The objective was to build strong local identities and create pathways for Indian music to reach audiences nationally and internationally, he explained.
According to Mr. Mehta, technology and data analytics are becoming central to the company’s strategy. Warner Music India analyses consumption patterns, geography, audience behaviour, catalogue performance, and the pace at which artists and tracks gain traction. These insights inform release strategies, marketing investments, and audience development, while helping identify commercial opportunities in partner labels’ catalogues.
The company’s Bengaluru technology hub is expected to strengthen these capabilities by bringing technology and engineering expertise closer to the markets it serves.
“We don’t believe Indian music needs to be made less Indian to become global,’’ Mr. Mehta opined. Local teams, data-led audience insights, and Warner Music’s international network can help independent Indian artists build on emerging momentum and reach overseas listeners.
Warner Music’s associations with Divo, Tips, Global Music Junction, and EYP bring regional expertise, repertoire, artist relationships, and market access. The company looks for strong local credibility, valuable intellectual property, and opportunities to add capabilities such as global distribution, technology, and artist development.
Over the next three years, Mr. Mehta said, more priorities would be placed on deepening regional presence, expanding services for artists and partners, and taking more Indian music to global audiences.
However, he observed, monetisation remained a significant industry challenge. While advertising continues to benefit from the scale of free listening, Warner Music sees paid subscriptions as a major growth opportunity. Mr. Mehta noted that 96% of smartphone users listen to music, while the paid subscriber base remained relatively small.
He argued that the industry must build a more diversified revenue model encompassing subscriptions, advertising, live performances, brand partnerships, publishing, and other rights, rather than depend on a single source of income.
For Warner Music India, Mr. Mehta further said, the long-term ambition was to combine local cultural understanding with global scale, positioning the company as a platform for artists to build sustainable careers.
India’s music industry is increasingly shaped by regional-language content, independent artists, and digital distribution, making it a market with substantial audience reach but considerable monetisation headroom. Converting free listeners into paying customers, developing intellectual property beyond film soundtracks, and expanding revenues through live entertainment, publishing, and brand partnerships would be important to building a more sustainable ecosystem for artists and rights holders, he observed.

stories.headline: OPEC cuts India’s 2026 oil demand growth forecast to 40,000 barrels per day
stories.deck: Gasoline and diesel to drive consumption amid strong vehicle sales, manufacturing and agricultural activity.
stories.bodyText:
The Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) has lowered its forecast for India’s oil demand growth in 2026 to 40,000 barrels per day (b/d), from 60,000 b/d projected in its September report.
On a year-on-year (YoY) basis, India’s oil demand is expected to rise by around 40,000 b/d to 5.7 million barrels per day (mb/d) in 2026, according to OPEC’s latest monthly oil market report.
OPEC has also trimmed its global oil demand growth forecast for 2026 to 0.2 mb/d, down from 0.4 mb/d estimated in its previous assessment. However, it has raised its projection for global oil demand growth in 2027 to 2.6 mb/d, from 2.4 mb/d forecast last month.
Its outlook for India’s oil demand growth in 2027 remains unchanged.
Transportation fuels to drive demand
Transportation fuels, particularly gasoline and diesel, are expected to remain the primary drivers of India’s oil demand growth in 2026.
“Gasoline is expected to be supported by heightened road mobility amid robust vehicle sales. Diesel demand is anticipated to gain additional support from strong manufacturing and agricultural activity,” OPEC said.
The report also projects an increase in demand for residual fuel during the year, while jet fuel consumption is expected to register marginal growth.
In contrast, demand for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and naphtha is expected to ease, OPEC said.

briefs.headline: IMF raises India growth forecast to 7%
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The 
International Monetary Fund
 (IMF) has upgraded India's growth forecast for the current year to 7%, from 6.4%, making it the fastest-growing major economy.
The agency joins others - including the World Bank, ADB, S&P and Moody's - in upgrading its projections after official data estimated first-quarter growth at 7.8%. Most global agencies have forecast 6.9-7% growth in the current fiscal year. IMF's latest World Economic Outlook estimated inflation at 5% this year with per capita output projected to rise 4.7% in 2026 compared with 5.2% last year.
It said that the global economy, projected to grow 3.4% in 2026, has stayed resilient despite multiple shocks in recent years. "India remains among the fastest-growing major economies, with growth in 2026 projected at 7%. This reflects stronger-than-expected momentum, supported by resilient domestic demand and robust services activity," the multilateral agency said.
India along with Germany has seen the highest revision, with Saudi Arabia forecast to contract 3.3% this year, seeing a five-percentage-point cut in the projection.
"India stands out with upward revisions, reflecting sustained momentum and growing evidence of stronger growth potential supported by favorable demographic dynamics, a large and expanding domestic market, and continued structural reforms," IMF said.
The report highlighted efforts to diversify trade flows and pointed to India's trade deals with the UK and the European Union that will lower tariffs and reduce barriers to services trade, and "facilitate adjustments to recent trade policy changes". US tariff actions have resulted in a flurry of trade deals across the globe, with India too moving ahead with FTAs that have been on the negotiating table for years.

briefs.headline: Now, MDR on UPI to be rolled out after Diwali
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Amid pushback from industry, National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has deferred the rollout of merchant discount rate (MDR) on select UPI transactions until after Diwali. In a statement on Tuesday, NPCI said that a new date of implementation will be notified separately. The merchant fee was earlier supposed to come into effect from Oct 15, amid the peak Navratri season when festive sales volumes surge.
Retailers heaved a sigh of relief as the move will spare them the need to reconfigure billing and accounting systems, besides briefing store staff at the point of peak footfalls.
"Deferment avoids this and gives the trade time to prepare.....the festive quarter is the single most important trading window for apparel retail. UPI has become the default payment mode at the store counter, and any change in the cost of accepting it directly affects checkout practices, reconciliation and consumer experience," said Santosh Katariya, president, Clothing Manufacturers Association of India (CMAI).
Payment companies recovered from early losses after NPCI confirmed that MDR implementation would begin immediately after Diwali. 
Paytm fell over 7% to Rs 1,571 before recovering 9.1% to close at Rs 1,714, up 1.5%. One MobiKwik Systems recovered from a 4% dip to close at Rs 245, up 1.7%, while Pine Labs rebounded from Rs 154.4 to Rs 164.8, gaining 1.1%.
Associations, however, urged govt to revisit the Rs 2,000 threshold given that a large share of apparel retail value (particularly for purchases made during weddings and festive) breaches that mark.
The MDR framework was approved by NPCI on Sept 15, with a 0.4% charge for eligible person-to-merchant UPI transactions above Rs 2,000, capped at Rs 300 for transactions of Rs 75,000 and above.
Kumar Rajagopalan, executive director & CEO at Retailers Association of India (RAI), said that the fee should ideally be a fixed amount rather than a percentage of the transaction value. He added that inflation has already been squeezing their margins.

briefs.headline: How phones on EMI are driving loan demand for two-wheelers
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Consumer durable loans, such as those for buying a mobile phone on EMI, are helping lenders build credit histories for younger borrowers, contributing to a decline in two-wheeler loan delinquencies to a seven-year low of 1.4% in June 2026 from 2.7% in June 2019, according to TransUnion Cibil.
First-time borrowers accounted for 39% of two-wheeler loan originations in the first half of 2026, down 19 percentage points from pre-pandemic levels. Meanwhile, 43% of borrowers had more than two years of formal credit history, up from 27% in 2019. Another 18% had less than two years of credit history, indicating more than 60% of borrowers had an established credit record, according to TU Cibil's latest report, Shifting Gears 2026: Credit Drives Today's Mobility.
Consumption-led borrowing has contributed to this shift. Nearly a third of two-wheeler borrowers had consumption credit products in their credit histories in the first half of 2026, up from 22% in the corresponding period of 2019. Consumer durable loans featured in the histories of 18% of borrowers and gold loans in 16%, credit cards in 12% and agriculture-related credit products in 8%.
NBFCs held 73% of outstanding two-wheeler loans.
