briefs.headline: Rupee up 49 paise, RBI governor says curbs to halt speculation
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: The rupee rose 49 paise to close at 95.28 per dollar on Tuesday from 95.77 in the previous session, outperforming Asian currencies after RBI introduced measures to curb dollar demand and speculative positions. The measures have widened bid-ask spreads in the forwards market and shifted some activity to the non-deliverable forward market.
Meanwhile, RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said the curbs were aimed at checking speculative bets against the rupee after the central bank found that around one-third of derivative trades were being cancelled or closed on the day they were entered into.
In an interview with Moneycontrol published on Tuesday, Malhotra said RBI had acted because speculative activity was amplifying currency volatility instead of serving genuine hedging needs. "We observed excessive volatility and one-sided bets that were preventing market forces from determining the rupee's true value," he said.
RBI announced a series of measures on Oct 10 after the rupee came under sustained pressure, touching a record low of 96.96 against the dollar on Friday. The steps included supplying dollars directly to three state-run oil marketing companies, tightening rules for foreign exchange derivatives and introducing a Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve requirement for banks on qualifying transactions. The governor said genuine hedging typically involved maintaining a position for the duration of the underlying exposure.

"...many decisions have been taken by various chairmen in the group, which have all proved to be right in the long-term. Sometimes if things go wrong, you course correct. Directionally you design it on the belief it is needed for India, it is needed for mankind, and for enterprises, you will get it right. He said that everyone recognises that chips are the future and the decisions were financially prudent. Direction is certain, the need is certain, the ability to execute is certain and the only thing is how you ramp up, how fast you ramp up..."
The comments come amid an intense boardroom battle, pitting Chandra and other board members against Tata Trusts chief Noel Tata, who had questioned the losses incurred in businesses, such as aviation and semiconductors, sectors where govt attention is also focused.

stories.headline: 'Abhishek was also taking a little time': Pujara explains why Samson struggled in 3rd T20I
stories.deck: Cheteshwar Pujara said Sanju Samson’s early dismissal for three in the third T20I against West Indies resulted from failing to read the pitch properly and accelerating too soon. He also praised Ishan Kishan for his effective role at No. 3, highlighting his ability to maximise the Powerplay and contribute valuable quick runs. India won by 14 runs, taking a 2-1 series lead.
stories.bodyText:
Former India batter 
Cheteshwar Pujara
 has explained why 
Sanju Samson
 struggled in the third T20I against West Indies in Indore. Samson, who scored an impressive 82 in the previous match, managed just three runs off six balls before being dismissed.
Despite his early exit, India scored 223/20, powered by 
Abhishek Sharma
’s 69 off 30 balls. West Indies fell 14 runs short, giving India a 2-1 lead in the five-match series.
Pujara explains Samson’s mistake
Speaking on JioStar’s show, GamePlan, Pujara felt Samson needed more time to understand the pitch conditions before attempting aggressive shots.
With Abhishek also taking time to settle, Samson was under pressure to score quickly. He was caught by Kamil Pooran off Shamar Joseph in the second over.
"He should have understood the wicket a little more. The phase had become like that because Abhishek was also taking a little time. So Sanju didn't have that option. He had to accelerate a little early, and that's why that error happened," on JioStar's show, 'GamePlan'.
"The bat turned in his hands. The ball was definitely good, there is no doubt about that, but I still felt that he might have batted better had he gotten a little more time," he added.
Pujara praises Ishan Kishan’s role
Pujara also praised Ishan Kishan for his contribution at No. 3, highlighting how the left-handed batter has helped India maintain momentum while supporting the explosive players at the top of the order.
"If we talk about Ishan Kishan, coming at No. 3, he is doing what the Indian team needs. You cannot see a big score every time because you have explosive players in the top order. Their role is to give the team a good start and to make the most of the Powerplay," he said.
"Whenever Ishan Kishan has come to bat, he has maximized the Powerplay. After that, you want to accelerate because you have wickets in hand. So, quickfire 30-40 is good enough. Maybe for his personal milestone, you might want him to score big runs, but he is doing the job for the team," he added.
India will face West Indies in the fourth T20I in Hyderabad on Wednesday, aiming to extend their series lead.

stories.headline: Hazlewood takes six as Australia beat South Africa in 1st Test
stories.deck: Fast bowler Hazlewood twice broke promising stands and finished with six for 49.
stories.bodyText:
Josh Hazlewood took six wickets as Australia completed a 214-run win over South Africa on the fifth day of the first Test at Kingsmead on Tuesday (October 13, 2026).
Fast bowler Hazlewood twice broke promising stands and finished with six for 49.
Player of the match Matt Renshaw scored 190 during the first innings as he ended a near-decade wait for a second Test century.
The hosts, set 421 runs to win, were bowled out for 206, in the first Test series between the teams in South Africa since the 2018 sandpaper scandal.
"It's a great way to kick off a series, particularly from the position we were on day one," the tourists' captain Pat Cummins said after they were 124 for six early on before controlling the rest of the fixture against the world Test champions.
Cummins added he was proud of the team for "clawing our way back, kind of grinding it out, and then once we had the lead, you know, not giving it back".
"I think our standards were very high for the last three or four days," he added.
South Africa skipper Temba Bavuma said his players needed to learn from the way Australia played after his first loss in 13 Tests as captain.
"They showed their experience, they showed their skill to get themselves into a very competitive position," Bavuma said.
"You don't want to give them that opportunity to play the game from the front.
"We had the opportunity to prepare as well as we could."
"I think a lot of the mistakes we made out there were mental," he added after South Africa's first Test in 11 months.
Record-breaker Smith
Opening batsman Aiden Markram defied the bowlers for a minute short of six hours, scoring 75 before he was ninth out, caught behind from an inside edge off Mitchell Starc.
The last four wickets fell for five runs in the space of 16 deliveries against the second new ball.
Markram and Wiaan Mulder (29) were largely untroubled as they batted through the first 110 minutes of the day.
But a double bowling change brought two wickets.
Mulder was caught down the legside by wicketkeeper Alex Carey off Hazlewood for 29 after a 139-minute innings during which he faced 110 balls.
Renshaw came on to bowl his off-spinners in the next over and with his first ball dismissed Kyle Verreynne for a single when the South Africa wicketkeeper played a forcing shot against a wide ball and edged a catch to Steve Smith at slip.
It was the continuation of a dream match for Renshaw, who top-scored in both innings with 190 and 82, then took his first Test wicket when he dismissed Bavuma on Monday.
It was Smith's fifth catch of a match in which he became the world record-holder for most catches by a fielder in Tests.
Smith was back in action after being off the field at the start of South Africa's innings on Monday following a blow on the head while batting.
Marco Jansen made 35 and added 45 with Markram before Hazlewood bowled him in the fourth over with the second new ball.
Three balls later Simon Harmer gloved a sharply lifting ball to Carey.
Australia were in trouble with the bat on the first day but dominated the rest of the match after Renshaw steered them to a first-innings total of 390.
South Africa will need to bounce back quickly in the second Test of the three-match series in Gqeberha starting on Sunday, when Bavuma hinted that key fast bowler Kagiso Rabada would likely be fit to play.

stories.headline: Martinez blasts Man United hierarchy; Rooney brands comments ‘disrespectful'
stories.deck: Lisandro Martinez criticised Manchester United’s hierarchy after their 2-0 Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid, calling for greater investment in the squad. Wayne Rooney condemned the defender’s public remarks as “disrespectful” to teammates, questioning his motives and suggesting the club take action. Former United player Ashley Young agreed recruitment must improve but insisted players…
stories.bodyText:
Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has sparked controversy after openly criticising the club’s hierarchy following a 2-0 Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid, with former United captain Wayne Rooney accusing the Argentine of being disrespectful to his teammates.
The defender’s post-match interview raised questions about United’s summer recruitment strategy and the club’s readiness to compete at the highest level. Martinez expressed frustration with the lack of further investment in the squad, suggesting that the club’s decision-makers should have done more after the team secured its return to the Champions League.
Speaking to Amazon Prime, Martinez said: “I have to control myself a lot. But sometimes it’s a reflection in the mirror of how is our club at the moment,” Martinez told Amazon Prime. “We did a fantastic season last season. And now we expect more from the top, from up, to bring more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well, and today also Atletico they have an amazing team and they deserved to win today.
“I expect more from our technical director. I would have to be honest, as the players, we have to do more, but it’s just important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night.”
United, under director of football Jason Wilcox, reportedly invested around $213 million during the summer transfer window, bringing in players including Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. Despite that spending, the club has endured a disappointing start to the campaign.
The defeat in Madrid extended United’s winless streak across all competitions to five matches. The team has managed just one Premier League victory and currently sits 13th in the standings.
Martinez also reflected on the contrast between last season’s progress and the team’s current struggles, expressing disappointment with the performance in Spain.
“Last season we did everything; we created the base to be an amazing team,” Martinez said. “It's annoying, disappointing to come here and I'm not seeing my team trying to get an amazing result here, it's disappointing.”
Atletico made an immediate impact, with Pablo Barrios scoring in the opening minute before Ademola Lookman added a second-half goal to secure the victory. The result has increased scrutiny on United head coach Michael Carrick as the club attempts to recover from its difficult start.
However, Martinez suggested that the focus on managerial changes overlooks other issues within the organisation.
“You start changing, changing, changing manager. But what about other areas?” Martinez said. “I can’t say more.”
Wayne Rooney questions Martinez’s motives
Rooney strongly disagreed with Martinez’s decision to air his frustrations publicly, arguing that concerns about recruitment and squad quality should be discussed internally rather than through the media.
Speaking on Amazon Prime after the match, the former United striker said: "I actually disagree as I thought it was a good performance.
"It's a difficult one because I always used to feel like I was outspoken as a player, and you want to have your opinion, but I think he's maybe gone too far; that should be down to the manager, and that should stay internal because the fans want to hear the players speak and they want to see them care.
"He clearly cares and wants the club to invest more money and more players, and if they do that, I think he'll be one of the players out the door if I'm being honest with his performances.
"His performances haven't been good enough but I think in some ways he is right, in terms of the club need to invest more at the top end of the pitch and in defence as well.
"I think it looks like that was a bit of an agenda from him because that doesn't mirror the performance. I thought the performance was better."
Although Rooney acknowledged that United need improvements in key areas, he questioned why Martinez chose that particular moment to make his concerns public.
"I think Martinez was very premeditated. Why is he doing the interview after this game? Has he put himself forward, I very rarely hear him speak.
"It looked a bit premeditated and something he spoke about with his team to get out there. It's sad because when you need everyone to stick together as players, you can't be told what's going on above you.
"So you need them players, the manager, the coaching staff to stick together when you're having a difficult time; otherwise, something like that will rip a dressing room apart.
"I think it's a bit disrespectful to his team-mates as well because he's disrespecting his team-mates, he's saying they're not good enough. So he's saying his team-mates aren't good enough, so it's disrespectful."
Rooney also suggested that captain Bruno Fernandes would be better placed to raise concerns on behalf of the squad, while insisting that any issues should be addressed privately.
"I think Bruno is probably the only one who has any right coming out and saying something like that if I'm being honest as captain. And even then, it should be behind closed doors if there are issues, which does happen.
"Players have conversations with the manager, the manager then has a conversation with the board, but that interview there, it's not going to help the situation the club is in at the minute.
"Now all that's going to bring is more noise around it, the players are unhappy, they're unsettled, they don't trust in their own team-mates, that's not going to help at all."
Rooney draws on his own experience
Rooney went further when discussing whether Martinez was attempting to reflect the frustrations of Manchester United supporters. While expressing appreciation for the defender’s ability, he pointed to his injury record and questioned whether he had done enough to speak on behalf of the squad.
"I don't think he's really connected with the fans since he's been here, to be honest, because he's been injured a lot.
"I actually like him, I think he's a good player, but he's been injured, so for the money the Man United pay for him, he hasn't given the service back really.
"From that point of view, that's not me being disrespectful, I just think he's had a lot of injuries and hasn't played that much.
"So I think he's trying to speak on behalf of the players if you like, but I think he's done it in the wrong way, as I said before, I think that should be from the captain if that's the case.
"For me, it's disrespectful to his teammates. I had a similar situation when I went in and asked Alex Ferguson about what players we were bringing in, and I apologised two days later.
"So I can speak from experience of what he's just done, I think it is very disrespectful, there's a lot of young players in that dressing room as well that need some guidance from experienced players."
Drawing on his own playing career, Rooney argued that experienced footballers have a responsibility to guide younger teammates, particularly during difficult periods. He also indicated that the club’s board may need to respond to Martinez’s remarks.
"The board have to look at that, and they probably have to take some action on that, because that's just disrespecting the whole football club.
"Yes, there's issues, everyone wants more players and better players, but this is the players you've got. As a player, you've got to get on with it.
"You've got to go and show why you're a World Cup winner, as I said before. So, I think the board have to either come out and speak on it, or maybe he's done that to flush them out and get them to speak to the fans, but I just think it's the wrong time, and it's not going to help anyone."
Ashley Young backs Rooney’s assessment
Former Manchester United player Ashley Young also questioned Martinez’s timing, agreeing that the club’s recruitment process needs improvement but stressing that players must take responsibility for their performances.
Young acknowledged that United could have strengthened other areas of the squad during the summer, particularly in attack and defence. However, he argued that rebuilding the team cannot happen all at once.
"Of course, there is a lot of it that the players are talking about it. We spoke before the game about how the club needed to invest more, but when they've invested in the midfield but what does he want?
"Go and buy a whole new team? They're not going to do that. They need to start in different positions. They could've bought up front or in defence but they didn't. He's just come off the pitch, emotions are running high, we know that.
"But we know the recruitment has to work, it has to be better but they've got to take time and do it. The players have got to take it upon themselves, 'we're the players that are in this team, we're the players that are in this squad and go out on the pitch.'
"They are the ones who have to go and produce and show what they're about. There's not going to be any change now until January."
With the January transfer window still some way off, United face mounting pressure to improve results with their existing squad.
Martinez’s criticism has highlighted concerns about recruitment and the club’s direction, but Rooney and Young believe that publicly airing such frustrations risks creating further divisions inside the dressing room at a time when unity is crucial.

stories.headline: Champions League: Atletico defeats struggling Manchester United

stories.bodyText:
Atletico Madrid eased to a 2-0 win over Manchester United in the Champions League on Tuesday (October 13, 2026) to pile pressure on Red Devils coach Michael Carrick.
Pablo Barrios pounced inside the first minute for Diego Simeone's side and after Leny Yoro's 74th minute red card set United back further, Ademola Lookman added another for the hosts in Madrid.
Man United have made their worst domestic start in 40 years and this league phase defeat in the Spanish capital was another blow, with the team now winless in five games across all competitions.
Carrick handed Carlos Baleba his first start for the club since arriving from Brighton this summer, as well as pushing captain Bruno Fernandes out to the right side.
Atletico were without their skipper Koke, after the death of his mother, while coach Simeone selected Julian Alvarez from the off for the first time this season at the Metropolitano stadium, after he tried to force a departure this summer.
"Defend what we love," Atletico fans ordered their supporters with a banner display before kick-off and the Rojiblancos were ahead after just 50 seconds.
Alex Baena found a way in behind United's defence and cut the ball across for Barrios, with Ayden Heaven unable to keep the midfielder's shot from crossing the line.
Bryan Mbuemo might have equalised for the visitors, nudging the ball through Cristian Romero's legs but firing just wide.
Alejandro Grimaldo came inches away from extending Atletico's lead with a free-kick which hit the angle between post and crossbar.
The hosts thought they had a second when Johnny Cardoso finished neatly from the edge of the box before half-time but the goal was disallowed after a VAR review showed the ball had struck Marcos Llorente's hand during the build-up.
Alvarez, yet to score this season for Atletico, hit the post early in the second half.
United rallied and Fernandes's lob drifted narrowly wide before the Portuguese playmaker hit the crossbar from the left of the box after a corner routine.
However the three-time European champions suffered a setback when defender Yoro was harshly dismissed after a VAR review for bringing down Canada striker Jonathan David as the last man.
It opened the door for Atletico to grab their second, with David foiled by goalkeeper Senne Lammens but London-born Nigeria international Lookman on hand to tuck home the rebound after 79 minutes.
Carrick withdrew playmaker Fernandes, looking ahead to the weekend visit to face rivals Leeds in the English top flight, where improvement is badly needed.
Atletico goalkeeper Jan Oblak saved from United substitute Matheus Cunha in the final stages but there was no way back for United.
Simeone's side were able to claim their first points after an opening defeat at Liverpool.

briefs.headline: WTC table: SA crash out of top two after Durban defeat; Where are India?
briefs.deck: South Africa faced a significant defeat against Australia by 214 runs in the first Test at Durban. This loss caused South Africa to drop to third place in the ICC World Test Championship standings. Australia, with nine wins from eleven matches, remains at the top of the table. Matt Renshaw was instrumental in Australia's success, scoring 190 runs in the first innings.
briefs.bodyText:
South Africa have slipped to third place in the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) 2025-27 standings following their 214-run defeat to Australia in the first Test at Durban. The result has strengthened Australia's position at the top of the table, while New Zealand have moved into second place.
The defending champions entered the series in second place but dropped to third after suffering their second defeat in five matches in the current WTC cycle. South Africa now have a points percentage (PCT) of 60.00, while New Zealand sit second with 72.22 per cent.
Australia, meanwhile, consolidated their position at the summit with nine wins from 11 matches, taking their points percentage to 81.82. Bangladesh and India occupy fourth and fifth places, respectively, with points percentages of 55.56 and 51.52.
Updated WTC 2025-27 standings
PCT: Percentage of points earned. Ded.: Points deducted.
Hazlewood, Renshaw power Australia to dominant Durban victory
Australia secured the 214-run win at Kingsmead after Josh Hazlewood produced a career-best performance of 6/49 on the fifth day. South Africa, chasing a target of 421, were bowled out for 206 despite Aiden Markram's fighting 75 off 237 deliveries and Marco Jansen's 35.
Hazlewood broke the hosts' resistance by dismissing Wiaan Mulder for 29 before removing Jansen and Simon Harmer in the same over. 
Mitchell Starc then ended Markram's determined innings, while Hazlewood claimed the final wicket by dismissing Anrich Nortje.
The foundation for Australia's victory was laid by Matt Renshaw, who scored a magnificent 190 in the first innings and followed it up with 82 in the second. Australia posted 390 before declaring their second innings at 314/6, setting South Africa a challenging target.
South Africa had managed 284 in their first innings but struggled to sustain their chase on the final day. The defeat also marked Temba Bavuma's first loss as South Africa's Test captain.
Renshaw was named Player of the Match for his outstanding contributions with the bat and ball. Australia now lead the three-match Test series 1-0.

briefs.headline: Ranji Trophy: Hamstring injury rules Mhatre out for six weeks
briefs.deck: Mhatre sustained the injury while batting on the opening day against Chandigarh
briefs.bodyText:
Mumbai’s promising opener and vice-captain Ayush Mhatre is set to miss at least six weeks of cricket after sustaining a suspected Grade 4 tear in his right hamstring during the team’s Ranji Trophy season-opener against Chandigarh at the Wankhede Stadium.
Mumbai Cricket Association president Ajinkya Naik confirmed on Tuesday that the 19-year-old’s recovery timeline would depend on further consultations between the Mumbai team’s medical staff and the BCCI’s Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Bengaluru.
Mhatre sustained the injury while batting on the opening day against Chandigarh. He did not take the field during either of the visitors’ innings as Mumbai registered an innings-and-155-run victory.
“It happened while running between the wickets. He looks very sad. He worked really hard in the off-season. He was doing rehab with me only at BKC and would come all the way from Virar, do his rehab and go back. It happens, it is part of the game, and we will try to motivate him,” Mumbai captain Siddhesh Lad said.
“We had two or three simulation games and club games, and also played at the BKC (Ground). He was looking fine for the last three or four matches, but he felt something in his hamstring while taking a second run.”
The setback comes barely six months after Mhatre injured his left hamstring while representing Chennai Super Kings in the Indian Premier League on April 18. That injury had ruled him out for three months. It is understood that he had also been troubled by the right hamstring during his rehabilitation at the CoE.

briefs.headline: El Clasico Legends In Kolkata: Barca and Real icons set for Salt Lake clash on Nov 25
briefs.deck: Kolkata will host Barcelona Legends vs Real Madrid Legends at Salt Lake Stadium on November 25, bringing El Clasico nostalgia to India. Luis Figo, Carles Puyol and Iker Casillas are among the names reportedly expected, though official squads remain unconfirmed. The exhibition follows last year’s meeting in Mumbai, where Real Madrid Legends won 2-0, and adds another chapter to Kolkata’s rich…
briefs.bodyText:
Kolkata is preparing for another taste of El Clasico, with Barcelona and Real Madrid legends set to bring their famous rivalry to India on November 25. The exhibition will give fans another chance to see former stars of the Spanish giants together on Indian soil, following Real Madrid Legends’ victory in Mumbai last year. With Luis Figo, Carles Puyol and Iker Casillas among the names reportedly expected, the contest could be a significant occasion for a city with a long relationship with world football.
Kolkata to host Barcelona vs Real Madrid Legends
West Bengal sports minister Indranil Khan announced on Tuesday that Barcelona Legends and Real Madrid Legends will meet at the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan, popularly known as the Salt Lake Stadium, on November 25.
The official squads have not yet been confirmed, although Portuguese great Figo, who represented both Spanish rivals during his playing career, and former Barcelona captain Puyol are among the prominent names expected to feature, alongside Spain’s World Cup-winning goalkeeper Casillas.
This will be the second time the two clubs’ legends have faced each other in India, following their meeting at Mumbai’s DY Patil Stadium last year. Real Madrid Legends won that contest 2-0, with former striker Fernando Morientes and David Barral scoring the goals.
The two sides also met in Miami earlier in 2026, playing out a 1-1 draw in which Martin Montoya scored for Barcelona and Álvaro Negredo found the net for Real Madrid. 
Their Kolkata encounter will now bring the exhibition rivalry to another Indian city, with the final line-ups still to be confirmed.
For supporters, the appeal lies in seeing familiar names from two of football’s most celebrated clubs share the same pitch again. Figo’s unusual connection to both sides adds another layer of interest, while the prospect of Puyol and Casillas appearing gives fans further reason to watch for the official team announcements.
Barcelona return to Kolkata after eight years
Barcelona’s visit will mark their first appearance in Kolkata since September 2018, when they faced Indian football giants Mohun Bagan at the same stadium. The Catalans won that match 6-0, with Javier Saviola, Roger Garcia, Pedro Landi, Jari Litmanen and Jofre Mateu among the scorers.
Kolkata has hosted some of football’s biggest names over several decades, earning a reputation as one of India’s most devoted footballing cities. One of its most memorable occasions came in 1977, when Brazilian legend Pelé led New York Cosmos against Mohun Bagan at Eden Gardens, while German giants Bayern Munich visited the city in 2008 to play the Kolkata club in a friendly.
The city also hosted Lionel Messi’s only appearance on Indian soil in 2011, when Argentina faced Venezuela at the Salt Lake Stadium. More recently, the venue staged high-profile international friendlies in early October 2026, as India faced five-time world champions Brazil and two-time World Cup winners Uruguay.
The November exhibition will add another prominent fixture to that history, bringing together two clubs whose rivalry has captivated football supporters across generations. Although the squads remain unconfirmed, Kolkata’s latest football occasion already has a clear attraction: another chapter of El Clasico, this time featuring the legends who helped make it famous.

briefs.headline: Root and Tendulkar: Two great players and their motto that has enriched the sport
briefs.deck: Joe Root needs 1,644 runs to overtake Sachin Tendulkar’s Test run record. An interesting catch-me-if-you-can is guaranteed between the greatest batters their respective countries have produced
briefs.bodyText:
Watching Sachin Tendulkar play his final Test innings in Mumbai, I turned to a friend and said confidently, “No one will ever break his aggregate record because no one can score 15,000-plus runs given the international schedule and franchise cricket, nor play 200 Tests.” Twelve years later, it appears I may have been wrong on one count, possibly both. One of Tendulkar’s contemporaries, England’s Joe Root, needs 1,644 runs to overtake him. He was younger than Tendulkar was at the 14,000-run mark.
Root turns 36 in December and might know that Tendulkar played 34 Tests after turning 37 (scoring 2,474 runs). Root will not need as many to overtake the Indian. An interesting catch-me-if-you-can is guaranteed between the greatest batters their respective countries have produced.
Longevity is an important measure of greatness. It speaks to skill, form, fitness, consistency, motivation, adaptability, goal-setting, and to a lesser degree, luck. I thought Tendulkar would struggle a few years after an elbow surgery had made it difficult for him to lift even a cup of tea, leave alone a cricket bat. Yet he had an amazingly productive run thereafter, digging deep into his reserves as a player who was the among the best the world had ever seen. Motivation, like faith, can move mountains.
Athletes slow down as they grow older, it’s a natural process. The power of the mind might reduce the speed of decline and extend a career. Then the unquantifiables take over. Motivation, mainly, but also the stomach for constant physical punishment, and keenness to break records and place your achievements beyond the reach of a generation or two at least.
Pressures of captaincy
Not surprisingly, captaincy can have a negative effect. Tendulkar didn’t enjoy it, although he had the best batter in the world — himself — in the team. “I even contemplated moving away from the sport completely,” said Tendulkar of his struggles with captaincy.
Root has said he had “an unhealthy relationship” with captaincy. Ben Stokes took over and briefly changed English cricket with the ‘Bazball’ style of attacking cricket he had developed with coach Brendon McCullum. Root loved batting in the new style, exhibiting strokes that had been dormant. After Stokes announced his retirement, Root was given the holding job while Harry Brook served his apprenticeship, and this time he relished the job. Perhaps he might yet give us the adult version of Bazball whether he leads or not.
As his career was winding down, Tendulkar had a couple of goals — playing 200 Tests, the 200th and final at home in Mumbai, and scoring a century of international centuries. Halfway through his career, Sunil Gavaskar had suggested that anything fewer than 15,000 Test runs for a man of Tendulkar’s talent would count as a failure, although he phrased it more gently. Records and figures are an inherent part of Indian cricket, but not so deeply ingrained in the English psyche.
Root’s admiration for Tendulkar is genuine. He told The Athletic this year, “It’s remarkable what Sachin Tendulkar achieved in the game. You have to believe me when I say that to even be in the conversation with him is enough for me. The guy made his Test debut before I was born and played in my Test debut! His longevity in itself is remarkable…”
When Root overtook Ricky Ponting (13,378) to become the second highest run-getter in Tests, Tendulkar said, “To have gone past 13,000 runs is a remarkable achievement, and he’s still going strong. When I saw him for the first time in Nagpur in 2012 during his debut Test, I told my teammates that they were watching the future captain of England. What impressed me most was the way he was able to assess the wicket and how he rotated the strike. I knew at that very moment that he would be a big player.”
“You always want to represent your country in the best possible light. (We must) be really good role models and good human beings.” That might have been something Tendulkar said (and probably did in different ways), but it is Root speaking on his return to captaincy. The crown, if it does pass, will not find a more honourable man to wear it.

briefs.headline: Harmanpreet — A leader who took India to uncharted terrains
briefs.deck: She is someone who has enjoyed captaincy. And it was a job she did rather well. She transformed the team and mentored and backed the new kids
briefs.bodyText:
She came. She led. She conquered. Now, she has stepped down.
So, the best captain Indian women’s cricket has ever had will no longer walk out to toss with the rival captain in an international game. Harmanpreet Kaur would be cherishing those walks to the middle, in the glare of the television cameras. She is someone who has enjoyed captaincy. And it was a job she did rather well, for all those talks about the need for change in captaincy in recent times.
Granted, she could not take India to the semifinals of the Women’s T20 World Cup in England three months ago. But, last year she had led India to an ODI World Cup triumph.
“Only Kapil Dev and M.S. Dhoni have done that,” former India captain Shubhangi Kulkarni reminds you over phone from Pune. “So she is in a very exclusive club. And she played a major role in the Indian victory as a batter, too. Everyone talks about Jemimah Rodrigues’ brilliant hundred in the semifinal against Australia, but Harmanpreet made 89.”
After losing the openers Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma inside 10 overs, it was the skipper’s 167-run stand for the third wicket with Jemimah that put India’s chase of a World-record breaking target. Harmanpreet knows how to make an impact in big games, and she certainly knows how to torment Australia, the best team in women’s cricket.
Even in her last appearance as a captain against the Aussies, in the league match at the T20 World Cup at Lord’s, she had cracked a 27-ball 56 that gave India at least a fighting chance in what was a must-win situation. But, a determined Australia, riding on a superb partnership with its champion all-rounders Ellyse Perry and Ashleigh Gardner, knocked India out of the competition, avenging the loss in the ODI World Cup.
That was indeed a big blow to Harmanpreet and her women. They were one of the favourites and were at least expected to make the semifinals, but the defeat to South Africa, earlier in the Group of Death, was always going to be costly.
Historic triumph
The Indians, however, won the historic Women’s Test at Lord’s, which was played right after the World Cup. And India totally outplayed England.
That was followed by the twin successes at the Asia Cup and the Asian Games. So Harmanpreet could end her captaincy on a high.
She admitted, through her widely read Instagram post, that the decision to step down was not easy. “The decision carries years of memories, emotions, sacrifices, and moments that will stay with me for the rest of my life,” she wrote.
“I have given everything I had to this team and to Indian women’s cricket — my blood, my sweat, my time, and many times, a part of my own game and personal ambitions. There were moments when I had to put my individual performance, my own growth, and what I wanted for myself aside, because I believed the team had to come first.”
She said she had to make some difficult decisions. “Decisions that were not always understood, not always easy, and sometimes came at a personal cost,” she explained. “But every decision I made was with one intention - to make this team better and to give other players the opportunity to grow, believe in themselves and become the best versions of themselves.”
Shubangi, one of the pioneers of women’s cricket in India, says Harmanpreet indeed was able to transform the Indian team with her leadership. “She has led India through a period of enormous changes,” she said. “From a team which was competing well, and expecting to do well, to becoming a team that wins major championships — she did it through some real high points and through some very low points, too. We have waited for a long, long time, for 50 years to win a senior ICC championship. There was a heartbreak in 2005 and then a bigger one in 2017 (India lost the World Cup finals). So what Harmanpreet’s Indian team did last year is indeed remarkable, and it is something she could always be proud about.”
Transformed the side
Biju George, who has worked with Harmanpreet as the fielding coach of the Indian team also rates her captaincy highly. “She was an aggressive captain who hated losing,” says the Thiruvananthapuram-based man whose wards include Sanju Samson. “As a captain, she has reminded me of Sourav Ganguly. Like he transformed the Indian men’s team, Harman did something similar with the women’s team.”
Biju also has always been in awe of her batting. “Her 171 not out against Australia in the semifinal of the 2017 World Cup in England is the best innings I have ever seen, by a male or a female cricketer, and I was lucky that I could watch it along with the Indian team,” he said.
“Harman is one of the earliest batters who brought in power to women’s cricket. We have many players who can hit hard now, but not at the time when she was doing it.”
And Harman could change the complexion of a game with those big shots. And she has been doing it for so long. Biju feels she could be scoring more runs after relinquishing the captaincy. “She could bat with more freedom,” he says. “And I think she has quit captaincy at the right time. Smriti also deserves to be a captain for a few years. And I also think it is good that they did not split the captaincy between formats. It is always to have just one captain. Multiple captains could create issues within the team.”
There isn’t, of course, a better option than Smriti to lead India in all formats. And she was quick to pay a tribute to Harmanpreet’s captaincy.
“It has been a pleasure playing with you for so many years,” Smriti wrote on social media. “Ten years of your leadership have been fantastic and together, we will strive to bring many more laurels for our nation.”
Smriti’s opening partner Shafali also spoke of how much Harmanpreet meant to her.
“Since the day I made my debut, you have always been there for me, on and off the field,” said the swashbuckling opener. “From guiding me through the early days to standing by me through everything, I have always known I could count on you.”
Those words from Shafali actually reveal something about Harmanpreet. She nurtured young talents — be it Shafali, Shree Charani or Kranti Gaud — and encouraged them always. One has seen her wax eloquent about those youngsters at press conferences several times. You could understand how much their successes meant to her.
She was excited to see the emergence of Kranti as a quality seamer that India desperately wanted. And she made Shafali bowl when not many were expecting her to. The emergence of Shafali as a spinner who could bowl at different stages of a match has given the Indian attack an excellent option. She has justified her captain’s faith in her with some fine spells.
Shubhangi feels Harmanpreet deserves credit for handling the transition period in Indian women’s cricket well. “She is the only player in the team from the time WCAI (Women’s Cricket Association of India), of which I was the secretary, was running the game,” she says. “We had to struggle for funds, and things were not easy at all for India’s female cricketers. Now there is money and opportunities for our players.”
Harmanpreet could always be proud about her role in taking women’s cricket forward. That is something nobody could take away from her. And that World Cup.
Captaincy matters in cricket. Harmanpreet has shown that, the way few women in international cricket have.

briefs.headline: Ranji Trophy | Accuracy was the best thing for me: Kukna
briefs.bodyText:
Rajasthan left-arm spinner Kukna Ajay Singh attributed his five for 51 against Tamil Nadu here on Tuesday to accuracy and pace variations.
“My accuracy was the best thing for me in this performance.
“The plan was to bowl in one area and not move away from it whatever the batters might try. I kept varying my pace so that it didn’t get easier for them,” he said.
The 29-year-old said he had worked on his undercut deliveries during the pre-season while continuing to focus on accuracy through spot-bowling practice.
He revealed that conversations with New Zealand left-arm spinner Mitchell Santner during his net-bowling stint with Mumbai Indians in IPL 2026 helped him refine his approach.
“We even used to train together, and I had quite a few conversations with him. You also learn a lot when bowling to Rohit Sharma,” he said.
“I asked Santner about his methods, especially given his height advantage. I worked on my variations and used them in this match. I got N. Jagadeesan out that way,” he said.

briefs.headline: East Bengal left to rue missed opportunities against Al-Shorta
briefs.bodyText:
East Bengal FC squandered a first-half lead to suffer a 3-2 defeat against Iraqi side Al-Shorta in its second Group-D outing of the AFC Champions League Two at Salt Lake Stadium here on Tuesday.
David Hmar scored twice in the first half to put East Bengal ahead twice. He opened the scoring in the seventh minute when he shielded an Al-Shorta defender to receive Hardik Bhatt’s centre and turned sharply to complete a spectacular finishing.
Al-Shorta equalised in the 14th minute through Ahmed Yahya, who headed in from a corner.
Despite enjoying less possession, East Bengal looked more threatening on the counter-attack, registering 10 shots of which seven were on target, compared to Al-Shorta’s solitary effort on target.
The hosts regained the lead in the 41st minute after goalkeeper Jalal Hassan parried Daniel Ramirez’s free-kick. Basim Rashid recovered the ball near the goal line and delivered a back-heel, allowing David to finish from close range.
David missed two further chances before half-time to complete his hat-trick, and those misses proved costly.
Al-Shorta struck twice in quick succession after the break to turn the match around.
Hussein Al-Saedi equalised in the 51st minute before Kingsley Kuku headed home a corner from Argentine substitute Cristian Barco two minutes later.
Al-Shorta were reduced to 10 men in the 76th minute when Abdoul Magid received his second yellow card.
East Bengal pushed for an equaliser but failed to break through the visitors’ disciplined defence, leaving the home side to rue missed opportunities and a costly second-half collapse.

briefs.headline: Ranji Trophy | Madhya Pradesh continues to call the shots against Jammu & Kashmir
briefs.bodyText:
Overcast conditions offered Jammu and Kashmir a glimmer of hope on Tuesday, but an uninspired bowling display and sloppy fielding meant the home side failed to make the most of the opportunity against Madhya Pradesh in its Ranji Trophy Group-A fixture.
Heavy rain forced an early end to the day’s play, but not before MP tightened its grip on the contest.
J&K managed just one wicket in the morning session at the Sher-i-Kashmir Stadium, conceding 70 runs in 30 overs.
Captain Shubham Sharma remained unbeaten on 51 (132b, 2x4, 1x6), with Atharva Mahajan on 35 (84b, 4x4), as MP reached 151 for five, extending its lead to 227.
The body language of the J&K players told its own story.
Having failed to capitalise on familiar conditions, the home side appeared to have let the game drift away despite an opportunity to fight back. After Auqib Nabi reignited hopes with two wickets the other day, J&K needed early breakthroughs to stay in contention.
However, neither Nabi nor Sunil Kumar could add to his wicket tally on Tuesday, as the bowlers struggled to maintain pressure and allowed MP to settle in.
The fielding did little to help, with missed opportunities and lapses allowing MP to consolidate its position.
It took nearly an hour for J&K to find its first breakthrough of the day, with Aryan Pandey caught at gully by Shubham Pundir off a Rohit Sharma delivery. By then, MP had already begun to frustrate the home attack.
Shubham took charge thereafter, bringing up another half-century and ensuring MP did not lose its way.
He forged an unbroken 64-run partnership with Atharva for the sixth wicket, steadily strengthening his team’s position.
With heavy rain forecast for Wednesday, MP’s first-innings lead gives it the edge in a contest where the weather could prove decisive.
